content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To eat a piece of birthday cake, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sift the all-purpose flour (2 minutes)
Step 2. Cream the butter and sugar together (10 minutes)
Step 3. Crack the eggs into a small bowl (1 minute)
Step 4. Soften the butter at room temperature (45 minutes)
Step 5. Preheat the kitchen oven to 350 degrees (15 minutes)
Step 6. Whisk the dry ingredients into the wet batter (5 minutes)
Step 7. Buy fresh ingredients from the grocery store (1 hour)
Step 8. Grease the circular cake pans (3 minutes)
Step 9. Measure out the vanilla extract (30 seconds)
Step 10. Beat the eggs lightly with a fork (1 minute)
Step 11. Zest a fresh lemon for flavor (2 minutes)
Step 12. Locate the mixing bowls in the cupboard (1 minute)
Step 13. Rinse the mixing bowls (2 minutes)
Step 14. Set out the cooling racks (30 seconds)
Step 15. Clear off the kitchen counter space (5 minutes)
Step 16. Read through the entire cake recipe (10 minutes)
Step 17. Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans (4 minutes)
Step 18. Prepare the buttercream frosting (20 minutes)
Step 19. Bake the cake in the oven (35 minutes)
Step 20. Let the cake layers cool completely (1 hour)
Step 21. Measure the baking powder and salt (1 minute)
Step 22. Clean up the flour spills on the counter (5 minutes)
Step 23. Double check the oven temperature (10 seconds)
Step 24. Take the milk out of the refrigerator (30 seconds)
Step 25. Wash the rubber spatula (2 minutes)
Step 26. Tap the pans to remove air bubbles (30 seconds)
Step 27. Put away the leftover flour and sugar (5 minutes)
Step 28. Set a kitchen timer (10 seconds)
Step 29. Organize the decorating supplies (10 minutes)
Step 30. Level the tops of the cooled cake layers (5 minutes)
Step 31. Wash the dirty mixing bowls (10 minutes)
Step 32. Check the pantry for sprinkles (2 minutes)
Step 33. Plug in the electric hand mixer (10 seconds)
Step 34. Remove the cake from the oven (1 minute)
Step 35. Invert the cake onto the cooling rack (2 minutes)
Step 36. Smooth the top of the batter with a knife (1 minute)
Step 37. Unpack the grocery bags (5 minutes)
Step 38. Place the first cake layer on a plate (30 seconds)
Step 39. Soften the cream cheese for the frosting (30 minutes)
Step 40. Light the birthday candles (1 minute)
Step 41. Apply a thin crumb coat of frosting (15 minutes)
Step 42. Spread the final layer of frosting (10 minutes)
Step 43. Measure the powdered sugar (3 minutes)
Step 44. Find the apron in the laundry room (2 minutes)
Step 45. Sing the Happy Birthday song (1 minute)
Step 46. Check the expiration date on the milk (30 seconds)
Step 47. Retrieve the cake server from the drawer (30 seconds)
Step 48. Decorate the edges with a piping bag (10 minutes)
Step 49. Wash your hands thoroughly (40 seconds)
Step 50. Slice the finished cake into wedges (2 minutes)
